## The same operations in three dimensions {#iv2-operations-3d .component-lesson .vector-lesson}

All the operations from 2D work the same way in 3D — there is just one extra component.

<div class="c-3d-rules">
<div><h3>Add or subtract corresponding components</h3><p><span data-math="\begin{bmatrix}a_x\\a_y\\a_z\end{bmatrix}\pm\begin{bmatrix}b_x\\b_y\\b_z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}a_x\pm b_x\\a_y\pm b_y\\a_z\pm b_z\end{bmatrix}"></span></p></div>
<div><h3>Multiply every component by the scalar</h3><p><span data-math="k\begin{bmatrix}a_x\\a_y\\a_z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}ka_x\\ka_y\\ka_z\end{bmatrix}"></span></p></div>
</div>

::: notes
A brief bridge to the hinge and Example 3.7: the geometric rules and component operations are unchanged, with an extra z-component. Ask students which component to calculate next; there is no new operation to learn. Addition and subtraction combine matching components; scalar multiplication affects every component.
:::
